ev_0005.summary: Circle circle_01 (center point_03 (283.7,297.3), r~236.2) passes through A, B, C, D (all within 0.2 px of r). Chords: AB (seg_02), AC (seg_03), BC (seg_04), BD (seg_06, snapped to B/D), CD (seg_07, snapped to C/D). seg_01 is the diameter AD (through point_03; |AD|=2r). Dashed seg_05 runs from B to the center point_03 (it passes through the center within ~1 px). point_02 (259.9,430.4) lies on both AD and BC (within ~0.3 px), so it is their intersection and AD is perpendicular to BC there (direction dot product ~0). Thales gives right angles at B (ABD) and C (ACD); these are geometric inferences, not verified by detect_right_angle_marker, so they are candidates only. Labels A,B,C,D are bound by bind_point_labels; point_02 and point_03 remain unlabeled.

ev_0007.summary: Independent visual check of the critic's symptom

evidence: The original shows a filled dot at approximately pixel (284, 297), with the letter 'I' to its right. The label is visible in the original, so the element exists there.
The dot sits on segment AD. A is at about (325, 65) and D at about (243, 529). At y≈297 the line AD gives x≈283, which matches the dot.
The dot is at the circle center. The circle spans about x 48–520 and y 60–533, so its center is about (284, 297). The dot coincides with it.
The dashed segment from B ends at the dot I in the original. It does not stop short of AD.
The critic's claim that I is about 2/3 of the way from A to D is not supported. In the original, I is at the midpoint of AD (t≈0.5), which is the circle center.
I did not receive the current render, so the render-side absence of the dot and label comes from the critic and diagnosis reports and was not checked against the render directly.
payload.instruction: Confirmed discrepancy: the original has a filled dot labeled 'I' at the circle center, which is the midpoint of AD. Add point I at the midpoint of AD (approximately the circle center, about (284, 297) in image pixels), draw it as a filled dot, and label it $I$ to the right. End the dashed segment BI at I. Do not place I at the 2/3 position suggested by the critic, since the original does not support it. Keep the other solid chords unchanged. Any numeric coordinates should be taken from the TikZ coordinate system of the existing A and D points, not from pixel values.

ev_0008.summary: Repair for critic discrepancies only. Added the missing interior point I, drawn as a filled dot and labelled 'I' to its right, at the midpoint of seg_AD. Derivation: midpoint of A[324.76,65.03] and D[242.79,529.70] is [283.78,297.37], which matches the existing unlabelled CV point point_03 [283.68,297.37] within 0.1 px and the circle_01 center [283.96,297.17] within about 0.3 px. Hence AD is a diameter and I is the circle center. The original image observation confirms a filled dot at about (284,297) with the letter I to its right. The critic's suggestion of a point about 2/3 of the way from A to D is rejected because it conflicts with the midpoint and center evidence and with the original. The dashed seg_BI terminates at this same point (offset about 0 px from the center and on AD), so the 'short of AD' claim is not supported and seg_BI is unchanged. Existing objects (circle_01, seg_01..seg_07, seg_AB..seg_CD, seg_BI, point_03, labels A-D, right-angle objects) are kept unchanged.

Note: the critic's '2/3 of the way from A to D' description conflicts with the GES, which places I at the midpoint; I followed the GES.
